title: WPMS/1793/2015 of M/s Sagar Stone Crusher Ranihat Chauras Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No. 1793 of 2015 (M/S)
M/s Sagar Stone Crusher ....... Petitioner
 versus
State of Uttarakhand & others ....... Respondents
Mr. Rajendra Dobhal, Sr. Advocate assisted by Mr. Vipul Painuly and
Mrs. A.M. Saklani, Advocates for the writ petitioner.
Mr. I.P. Kohli and Ms. Anjali Bhargava, Brief Holders for the respondent
State.
U.C. Dhyani, J.(Oral)

By means of present writ petition, the
petitioner seeks a writ, order or direction in the nature of
certiorari quashing the impugned order dated 02.07.2015,
passed by respondent no. 2.
2) The facts giving rise to the present writ
petition are that petitioner is running a stone crusher in
the name and style M/s Sagar Stone Crusher at the place
of Village Ranihat Chauras, Tehsil Kirti Nagar, District
Tehri Garhwal since 2008, and has been granted
permission to operate the aforesaid stone crusher by the
competent authority from time to time and permission
granted to the petitioner is upto 31st March 2016. On
27.05.2014, District Magistrate, Tehri Garhwal
(respondent no. 3) has also issued a license to the
petitioner for storage of the minerals for two years w.e.f.
27.05.2014 upto 06.05.2016. The stone crusher of the
petitioner was inspected on 08.09.2013 by the five
member Committee constituted by respondent no. 3, vide

2
order dated 04.07.2013 and after spot inspection on
08.09.2013, the Committed submitted its report
recommending the permission to operate the Stone
Crusher of the petitioner as the same is being run
according to the Policy of the year 2011. Despite the
aforesaid joint inspection report, recommending the
permission to operate the stone crusher by the petitioner,
on 02.07.2015, respondent no. 3 suddenly passed the
impugned order, whereby the petitioner has been stopped
from operating his stoner crusher on the ground that
petitioner is not fulfilling the standard fixed under the
Policy of 2011, i.e., "Uttarakhand Ke Parvatiya Kshetra
hetu Stone Crusher, Screening Plant Evam Palvarizer
Annugya Neeti, 2011". Policy of the year 2011 was also
extended upto 2016, vide order dated 25.06.2014.
3) In the year 2013, a writ petition (PIL) no. 166
of 2013, Km. Seema Bharti vs State of Uttarakhand and
others was filed before this Court challenging the
operation of the stone crusher in the area and the
petitioner was also arrayed as respondent no. 5. In the
said writ petition, District Magistrate, Tehri Garhwal,
who was arrayed as respondent no. 2, filed his affidavit
stating therein that the stone crusher of the petitioner has
been operating in accordance with the Policy of 2011 and
the petitioner is fulfilling all the conditions and standards
given in the said Policy. Impugned order dated
02.07.2015 has been passed by the respondent no. 2,
without giving any show cause notice or opportunity to

3
the petitioner and as such, is illegal and violative of the
principles of natural justice. The Joint Inspection
Committee, which was constituted under the order of the
respondent no. 3, has given its report after the spot
inspection on 08.09.2013, stating therein that the
petitioner's stone crusher is fulfilling all the conditions
and standards given in the policy of 2011, but while
passing the impugned order dated 02.07.2015, the
respondent no. 2 has not taken into consideration the
aforesaid split inspection report. Hence, the present writ
petition.
4) Learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf
of the petitioner confined his prayer only to the extent
that the petitioner ought to have been given due
opportunity of hearing before passing the impugned order
dated 02.07.2015. This Court, therefore, proceeds to
decide the writ petition, with the consent of learned
counsel for the parties, only on the basis of such
submission made by learned Senior Counsel for the
petitioner.
5) It is true that the order impugned
nowhere mentions that any 'show cause' was given
to the petitioner before passing the impugned order.
6) It will be very useful to reproduce here-in-below some important observations made in
'Administrative Law', by H.W.R. Wade QC LLD FBA

4
published by the English Language Book Society
(ELBS)/Oxford University Press , 5
th
Edition, reprinted
in 1986, at page 469:
 "Time and time again in the cases I have cited it
has been stated that a decision given without regard to
the principles of natural justice is void and that was
expressly decided in Wood vs. Woad (1874) L.R. 9
Ex.190. I see no reason to doubt these authorities. The
body with the power to decide cannot lawfully proceed
to make a decision until it has afforded to the person
affected a proper opportunity to state his case. ... ... ...
... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... .... ... ...
... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... And Lord Modson held
that all authority was to the effect that a decision
contrary to natural justice was void, being vitiated by
'a want of jurisdiction', (1964) A.C. at p.136 Decisions
to the same effect are very numerous. One example is
R. v. North ex p. Oakey (1927) K.B. 491 at 503, 505
(Scrutton and Atkin L.JJ.). ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ...
... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... ...... ... ... ...
... ... ... ... ... ... ... ... The confusions in this case are
inextricable; ................................., since both the
House of Lords {Anisminic Ltd. v. Foreign
Compensation Commission, (1969) 2 A.C. 147;
Hoffman-La Roche v. Secretary of State of Trade and
Industry, (1975) A.C. 295} and the Privy Council {A.G.
v. Ryan, (1980) A.C. 143} have since reaffirmed that an
order made contrary to natural justice is outside
jurisdiction and void, and that any other terminology
would be 'inconsistent with the doctrine of ultra vires,
as it has been developed in English law as a means of

5
controlling abuse of power by the executive arms of
government."
[Emphasis supplied]
7) This Court, is therefore, of the opinion that
the petitioner ought to have been given a 'show cause'
before passing the impugned order. The impugned order,
therefore, suffers from non-compliance of principle of
natural justice, i.e., Audi alteram partem, which means -
nobody should be condemned unheard, which is not only
applicable to judicial organs but is also applicable to
quasi-judicial and administrative wings of the
Government. The same is liable to be kept in abeyance
on this ground alone.

8) Writ petition is allowed. Impugned order
dated 02.07.2015 is kept in abeyance for a period of three
weeks. Competent Authority is requested to pass an
order, after giving a show cause notice to the petitioner,
in accordance with law, within three weeks from today.
9) Let copies of this judgment be supplied to
learned counsel for the parties today itself on payment of
usual charges.
